text:
Hey Nick,
Apologies in the late reply.
I’ve added a spreadsheet to your Gdrive folder. I was considering moving various video samples however, it will break the links found in the spreadsheet. To simplify, you or your team can follow the individual samples to our own Gdrive where the video samples are hosted.

To remind you of the goal, we are using multi-modal models to classify break dancing moves focusing on two specific questions:

  *   Can AI identify top level taxonomy moves (toprock, footwork, freezes) which vary greatly in form and execution?
  *   Can AI identify small nuances in execution across variations of windmills?

In the spreadsheet you will find the human labeled samples, links to the associated video files, and a tab with the written descriptions of the poses.

We are looking for software that can support us with:

  *   The video annotation process
  *   Vision fine tuning
  *   Testing video classification accuracy
  *   Latency of such classification
  *   Model evaluation

Talk to you soon,

Max

subject: Re: UPDATE: Slice Sync in Encord
text:
Hi Seif,

Many Thanks for this update.

I've tested the functionality you shared by loading 2 X DICOM series on a custom layout, a primary- and a secondary capture, with ~200 vs 4 x slices, respectively.

As discussed, after the sync-browsing is enabled, browsing the secondary capture axial-slices, should navigate to the corresponding primary capture axial-slices, via the 'Slice Location Header information' (z-coordinate geometrical information), available on both DICOMS.
Here is a exemplar video with the proposed functionality working on Stone-Viewer (open-source, https://www.orthanc-server.com/static.php?page=stone-web-viewer):

[https://res.public.onecdn.static.microsoft/owamail/hashed-v1/scripts/../resources/images/stream-hash-047638c0.m.svg]Stone Viewer - DICOM Series Sync Browsing_v2.mp4<https://optellum-my.sharepoint.com/:v:/p/mauro_santos/EdJWMvnpuhpKid-X-tNwGU8BA93490qzMz5XXPfl16qCKw?nav=eyJwbGF5YmFja09wdGlvbnMiOnt9LCJyZWZlcnJhbEluZm8iOnsicmVmZXJyYWxBcHAiOiJTdHJlYW1XZWJBcHAiLCJyZWZlcnJhbE1vZGUiOiJtaXMiLCJyZWZlcnJhbFZpZXciOiJwb3N0cm9sbC1jb3B5bGluayIsInJlZmVycmFsUGxheWJhY2tTZXNzaW9uSWQiOiIxM2E0MzdiZC1mYTg5LTQ3MjAtOGZkNi1mYTc2MjIxZDZiOGMifX0%3D>

However, Encord's sync functionality just moves the slices up/down and does not guarantee Z-location syncing between the DICOMs Axial-views, which is different from our use-case.

Please let us know in case we missed something, otherwise our questions would be:
- if the DICOM Synced Browsing, based on the 'Slice Location Header' (z-coordinate), is part of Encord's roadmap?
- (if so) when would it became available on the Annotation platform?

In case something is not clear with our use-cases/descriptions, we would be happy to discuss this on a call, as it would be crucial to use this in our next trial.

Many Thanks,
Best Wishes,
Mauro

subject: Re: UPDATE: Slice Sync in Encord
text:
Hi Seif,

Thank you for clarifying.

For our study, syncing via the z-coordinate is a must have to:
(i) measure correctly the CT-scan aided-read (annotation) time;
(ii) facilitate AI Secondary Capture (SC) interpretation;
both being deteriorated otherwise.

(i) the Encord platform does a great job in providing the annotation timings!
However, the use of the average aided-read time derived in this study will be limited, as unfortunately it would not be comparable to the time gains versus
using a DICOM viewer that implements the sync browsing based on the z-coordinate.

(ii) This user pain point may also explain some of the results we're seeing in our current pilot, e.g. in CT-scans with several lesion/nodule findings in the AI SC,
some may be missed by the readers, as it's not efficient to scroll the CT-scan and SC independently
(i.e. as they try to scale the annotation workflow to hundreds of CT-scans).

Please let us know if we can provide more input towards the implementation of this functionality for the DICOM annotation tool.

Best Regards,
Mauro

Research Scientist
